summary: Iter43 verification of EsignWizard.tsx component split (Phase 42). PARTIAL VERIFICATION COMPLETED. Step 1 (Upload) was fully verified: all data-testids render correctly (step-pip-1..5, wizard-back, wizard-next, step-1-upload, doc-title-input, pdf-upload-zone, pdf-upload-input), Continue button is correctly disabled until BOTH title is typed AND PDF is selected, and the file selection updates the UI (file name + size). Code review confirms EsignWizard.tsx is 692 lines as claimed, imports WizardStepUpload/WizardStepSigners/WizardStepSettings from sibling files, uses shared wizardTypes.ts (SignerDraft, FieldDraft), and all data-testids referenced in the request are present verbatim in the extracted child components. HOWEVER, Steps 2, 3, 4 functional verification + autosave-restore test are BLOCKED: the Step 1 → Step 2 transition calls POST /api/esign/documents which returns 500 because asyncpg cannot connect to PostgreSQL at 127.0.0.1:5432 ([Errno 111] Connect call failed). PostgreSQL is not installed/running in this preview pod — no `postgres`, `psql`, `pg_ctlcluster` binaries; no postgresql Debian package. The eSign backend hard-depends on PG (Phase 38 schema). The refactor itself is NOT the cause — same upload would have failed before the split. This is an environment bootstrap regression vs prior iterations (per iter42 note, PG was previously bootstrapped).

critical.issue: Returns 500. asyncpg/SQLAlchemy cannot connect to PostgreSQL at 127.0.0.1:5432 — [Errno 111] Connect call failed. PG is not running in this preview pod (no postgres binary, port 5432 not listening). This blocks the entire eSign wizard at Step 1 → Step 2 transition and prevents verifying Steps 2/3/4 functionally.

Caused by missing PostgreSQL — not a frontend bug, but error UX is silent.

action_items: CRITICAL (infra): Restore PostgreSQL in this preview pod and re-run the eSign DB bootstrap (Phase 38 schema: documents, signers, signature_fields, audit_events) so /api/esign/* endpoints can actually serve requests. PG is currently not installed (no binaries, port 5432 not listening). Without this, the eSign wizard is fully blocked beyond Step 1.

Verify the toast actually surfaces a visible error to users when the backend errors — silent failure on click is bad UX.

After PG is restored, re-run this iteration's Step 2/3/4/autosave-restore scenarios. The refactor's structural integrity is already verified via code review; only functional verification of the post-Step-1 flow is outstanding.
critical_code_review_comments: EsignWizard.tsx — clean orchestrator pattern; child components receive only the state + setters they need (good prop-drilling discipline). Shared types via wizardTypes.ts avoids cycle.
WizardStepUpload.tsx (61 lines) — pure JSX, no side effects, accepts (title, setTitle, file, onFile) — good split.

WizardStepSigners.tsx (172 lines) — owns drag/drop reorder logic, which slightly violates 'pure JSX' (it mutates parent's signers via setSigners on drop). Acceptable since the state is parent-owned, but the drop handler could be lifted to the parent for a cleaner split.
WizardStepSettings.tsx (95 lines) — pure render of summary + 3 controls, clean.
wizardTypes.ts — minimal shared type file, correctly imports FieldType from './api' to avoid duplication.

Silent failure on upload 500: handleFile/uploadAndContinue should surface a non-default destructive toast even when e.message is undefined/empty. Currently toast({ title: 'Upload failed', description: e.message, variant: 'destructive' }) — description may be empty when fetch throws a generic error.
useMemo at line 500 is used purely for its side-effect of calling setActiveSignerId — incorrect hook usage. Should be useEffect. Pre-existing, not introduced by this refactor.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of the Step 1→2 failure: asyncpg.connect() raises OSError [Errno 111] Connect call failed ('127.0.0.1', 5432) because PostgreSQL is not running (or installed) in the current pod. Backend log shows SQLAlchemy pool._create_connection() bubbling this up, returning 500 to the client. Reproduction: login → /tools/esign/new → type title + select PDF → click Continue → observe POST /api/esign/documents 500 in network log. Mitigation: install PostgreSQL (apt-get install postgresql) or start the existing PG service, then run the eSign migrations to create the documents/signers/signature_fields/audit_events tables. The refactor itself is unaffected by this — same error would occur in the pre-split codebase.
